name: Pitch Deck
description: An investor or partnership pitch deck following a classic narrative arc
layout_notes: Target 12–15 slides. Every slide should earn its place. No bullet soup — use large statements and supporting visuals. Follow the Guy Kawasaki / Sequoia narrative arc: problem → solution → market → traction → team → ask.

required_sections.title: Title Slide
required_sections.description: Company name, tagline, logo, presenter, date

required_sections.title: The Problem
required_sections.description: Make the pain visceral and relatable — use a story or stat

required_sections.title: Our Solution
required_sections.description: The 'aha' moment — clear, visual, and memorable

required_sections.title: The Product
required_sections.description: How it works — screenshots, demo, or diagram

required_sections.title: Market Opportunity
required_sections.description: TAM / SAM / SOM or equivalent — why this is a big opportunity

required_sections.title: Traction
required_sections.description: Revenue, users, growth rate, key customers, notable milestones

required_sections.title: Competitive Landscape
required_sections.description: Positioning vs alternatives — be honest and specific

required_sections.title: The Team
required_sections.description: Why this team can win — relevant experience and track record

required_sections.title: Financials
required_sections.description: Current ARR/MRR, burn, runway, and 3-year projections

required_sections.title: The Ask
required_sections.description: Raise amount, use of funds, and what you're looking for in a partner

optional_sections.title: What Customers Say
optional_sections.description: 1–2 strong customer quotes or case study stats
